summary: Modifies the previous policy for scheduling IMP and TIP down time.

eli5.summary: The network boxes sometimes needed to be turned off for work. This note changes the rules for planning when.

subtitle: How the network planners notified sites about scheduled maintenance on switching nodes and terminal interfaces

tldr.problem: The network needed to take down IMPs (Interface Message Processors) and TIPs (Terminal Interface Processors) for maintenance and repairs, but the previous notification policy did not reach all affected organizations.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC modifies the policy to allow any host organization to nominate a secondary contact who will be notified by telephone when their IMP or TIP is scheduled for downtime, in addition to the primary site contact.
tldr.outcome: This gave individual organizations better visibility into planned maintenance that affected their operations, adapting the notification system to the growing network.

today: RFC 622 is an Unknown status memo from March 1974 describing an operational policy for ARPANET maintenance notification.

sections.title: The Notification Problem
sections.content:
From time to time, network switching nodes called IMPs and TIPs needed to go offline for maintenance: retrofit programs, repairs of intermittent problems, and scheduled preventive maintenance. The Network Control Center had previously coordinated these downtimes by contacting only the primary site contact at each installation, trusting them to represent all the hosts and users connected there.

As the network grew with many distant hosts spread across different organizations at single sites, this approach left many users and administrators in the dark about upcoming maintenance.
sections.eli5: When a network box needed work, the bosses only told one main contact person at that site. But if many different groups used that same network box, the others might not find out.

sections.title: The New Secondary Contact System
sections.content:
The RFC modifies the policy to allow any host organization to nominate a secondary contact. This person would receive a telephone notification after the Network Control Center schedules the downtime with the primary contact.

Organizations could submit the secondary contact's name and telephone number through three methods: US mail to the Network Control Center at BBN in Cambridge, the ARPANET journal system (ident AAM), or network mail to MCKENZIE at BBN-TENEX.
sections.eli5: Now any group at a site could say: please also call this person when there's maintenance scheduled. The network would call them on the phone.

sections.title: Impact and Historical Context
sections.content:
The RFC includes a comprehensive list of the primary site contacts at 34 network locations, from UCLA and Stanford to international sites like London and NORSAR. This mechanism represented an early attempt to scale notification procedures as ARPANET grew from a few dozen nodes to a larger, more distributed system with multiple autonomous organizations at single sites.

The policy reflected the operational challenges of coordinating maintenance across a growing network where human communication and notification were still the primary mechanisms for coordination.
sections.eli5: The list showed all the main people they called about maintenance. This change helped as the network grew bigger and had more organizations sharing the same equipment.
